title: Wire a door-mounted lamp across the hinge of a junction box and latch the door
instruction: Wire the door lamp to the socket inside the junction box, fixing its cord in the cable clip, and latch the door shut.
context: A standard small sheet-steel junction box (catalogue size 200 x 150 x 80 mm) with a 22 mm pilot lamp in its door, at its real size. Wiring door-mounted lamps and switches into enclosures is routine panel and box-build work for electricians (O*NET 47-2111) and for the team assemblers and electrical equipment assemblers who build control panels (51-2092, 51-2028). The cord crosses the hinge, so it has to be clipped inside the box: a cord left across the rim is crushed in the seam when the door shuts. Plug, lamp and clip are joined by one flexible cord, so seating the plug and clipping the cord each pull on the other. After the robot lets go, the door is opened to its stop and shut again, as an inspector would, to show the wiring survives the swing. In the simulation and in the videos the door moves by itself during this test: it is the scripted inspection, driven by the task file, not the robot. The push-in plug stands in for a pluggable door-device connector and holds more weakly.
setup: Positions in cm: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left of the midline, z up from the bench top. (1) Junction box: light grey powder-coated sheet-steel junction box, 20 (x) x 15 (y) x 8 cm outside, 1.2 mm sheet; it lies on its back on the bench for wiring, screwed down, x 17 to 37, y -10 to +5. (2) Door: 20 x 15 cm, 1 mm steel, 0.28 kg with the lamp, hinged along the box's left long edge (the hinge line runs along x at y +5, z 8); it opens 0 to 120 degrees (a stop at 120) with a 0.35 N m friction hinge that holds it where left. It starts standing upright, open 90 degrees. (3) Pilot lamp: red 22 mm LED panel indicator (30 mm chrome bezel) in the door, its centre 2 cm from the door's near edge (x 19) and 4.5 cm from the hinge line, 32 mm deep behind the door. (4) Cord: black 5 mm round PVC two-core cord, 30 cm from the back of the lamp to the plug. It starts straight out of the back of the lamp, across the open box and over the front (y -10) wall, its far end lying on the bench. (5) Plug: black two-pole connector plug with its strain-relief boot, 44 x 15 x 12 mm, 12 g, no latch, lying flat on the bench at x 19, y -27, tip pointing away from the box (-y). Real trials: a black PETG body printed from hardware/plug_body.stl, the cord's end glued into its rear channel, 11-13 g, a white line 12 mm from its tip. (6) Panel socket: dark grey block 22 x 29 mm, its top 23 mm above the bench (21 mm above the 2 mm back plate it stands on); its cavity (19 mm wide, 15 mm tall, 16 mm deep, 4 mm lead-in) opens toward the robot at x 33, centred at y -3.5, 1.3 cm above the bench; a sprung contact in the roof holds a seated plug (about 1 N to pull it out). Real trials: no catalogue part has this latch-free 1 N fit, so it is made: socket body and contact pad printed in PETG from hardware/socket_body.stl and socket_pad.stl, pressed down by a 0.10 x 6 x 20 mm AISI 301 stainless shim strip glued on the roof (0.40 N/mm, 0.4 N preload; the pad's flange and the strip stand 1.1 mm above the block), taped to the back plate; dimensions, tolerances and acceptance checks (pull-out 0.7 to 1.3 N on a push-pull gauge) in hardware/drawing.pdf. (7) Cable clip: a HellermannTyton RB5-PA66-NA (article 151-14059) one-piece adhesive snap-in cable clip, natural off-white PA66, 19 x 19 mm and 6 mm tall, 9.7 mm across its arms, for cable up to 5 mm (maker's sizes), stuck on the back plate centred at x 26.8, y -3.35, its channel along x (x 25.85 to 27.75). Its arms stand 5.5 mm apart; a lip on one arm, 3.9 mm above the channel floor, narrows the entry to about 4 mm, so a 5 mm cord pressed in spreads the arm and snaps under the lip, lying flush with the arm tops. Arm and lip sizes and the grip are our estimates: the maker publishes no holding force. (8) Catch: a spring bolt in a 24 x 8 x 24 mm housing inside the front wall at x 27, and a hook under the door's free edge: pushing the door shut (about 5 N at its free edge) clicks the bolt over the hook. The layout is identical every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged with a ruler and a photo. Terms: plug seated = in line with the socket, its tip at least 12 mm inside (a mark 12 mm from the tip is hidden); cord clipped = the cord lies under the clip's lip, between its arms, along the clip's whole length; latched = door shut with the catch bolt over its hook; hands clear = no part of either gripper within 3 cm of the box or of the door's swing (up to 26 cm above the bench). Ladder, each rung needing all the ones below it and hands clear: 0.2 plug seated; 0.4 cord clipped; 0.6 door latched. Door test, once 0.6 has held, all still, for 1 s: an inspector presses the catch, swings the door by hand to its 120 degree stop over 2 s (at most 0.8 N m, about 6 N at the free edge), holds it 1 s, swings it shut and pushes until it clicks (in simulation the task file drives the hinge the same way). 0.8: the door reached at least 115 degrees with the plug seated, the cord clipped and hands clear the whole time. 1.0: once the test has ended (7 s after it began), the door is latched again with the plug seated, the cord clipped, no cord outside the box's walls and hands clear, and all of this has held, everything still, for a further 1 s; until then the score stays 0.8. A cord trapped during the door test scores zero, not 0.6 or 0.8. A failed door test otherwise leaves the score at 0.6 (or 0.8 if only the re-shutting failed). A plug pulled below 12 mm during the door test is a failed test, not a cap: 0.8 if it stayed seated until the door had reached 115 degrees, else 0.6. Zero, whatever else happened: the cord was ever outside the box's walls (across the rim) while the door was within 8 degrees of shut; or the door came within 8 degrees of shut before the plug was first seated. Cap: at most 0.2 once the plug has been below 12 mm at any moment after it was first seated and before the door test began. Any end state matching no rung scores 0.
reset_notes: Pull the plug out, free the cord from the clip, lay the cord straight from the back of the lamp across the box and over the front wall with the plug flat on the bench (tape mark), stand the door upright at 90 degrees and check the catch bolt is out. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies. Cord: 20 rigid 15 mm links with bending springs, no twist or stretch, welded to the lamp; its slack across the hinge is fixed by the clip's position. Clip: the commercial RB5 at its catalogue size; its flexing arm is a sprung slider (0.6 N/mm, 0.6 N preload: our estimate). Socket pad: sprung slider, grip by friction, no latch. Catch: sprung bolt and hook. Hinge friction: capped spring. The door test is the task file driving the hinge. Sheet 2 mm thick.
